where: Section 3, von Mises formulas (also the plane-stress forms in step 7 and quiz Q4)
problem: The exponents are typed as plain digits, so the formulas read 'σvm = √(0.5[(σ1 − σ2)2 + (σ2 − σ3)2 + (σ3 − σ1)2])' and 'σvm = √(σ12 − σ1σ2 + σ22)' and '√(σx2 − σxσy + σy2 + 3τxy2)'. A reader sees σ12 or (σ1 − σ2)2, not a square, and the formula becomes wrong as printed.
fix: Use superscript markup everywhere: σ<sub>vm</sub> = √(0.5[(σ<sub>1</sub> − σ<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + (σ<sub>2</sub> − σ<sub>3</sub>)<sup>2</sup> + (σ<sub>3</sub> − σ<sub>1</sub>)<sup>2</sup>]); plane stress σ<sub>vm</sub> = √(σ<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> − σ<sub>1</sub>σ<sub>2</sub> + σ<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>) and σ<sub>vm</sub> = √(σ<sub>x</sub><sup>2</sup> − σ<sub>x</sub>σ<sub>y</sub> + σ<sub>y</sub><sup>2</sup> + 3τ<sub>xy</sub><sup>2</sup>).

problem: 'Using σx and σy directly in Tresca or von Mises. Both theories need the principal stresses' contradicts section 3, which gives a von Mises formula straight from σx, σy and τxy. von Mises can be computed from the given components; the real mistake is leaving out τxy, or using σx − σy directly in place of σ1 − σ3 for Tresca.
fix: Tresca needs the principal stresses, with σ3 = 0 included in plane stress, because it uses σ1 − σ3. von Mises may be found from the components only if τxy is kept: σvm = √(σx² − σxσy + σy² + 3τxy²). Dropping τxy or using σx − σy where σ1 − σ3 is required gives a wrong answer.

problem: The theory is defined but never given its second standard name, so a student meeting 'maximum shear stress theory' in an exam question may not connect it to Tresca.
fix: Add: 'Tresca theory, also called the maximum shear stress theory, says failure occurs when the maximum shear stress reaches the shear yield strength, σY/2.'

where: Section 2, Rankine paragraph (and Section 1 definition of σY)
problem: Rankine is applied with the yield strength σY, but cast iron and concrete do not yield; standard treatments compare the largest principal stress with the ultimate tensile strength (or the ultimate compressive strength when the largest stress is compressive). Using σY for a brittle material is inconsistent with the material behaviour the paragraph itself describes.
fix: State that for brittle materials the limiting stress in Rankine is the ultimate strength (σut in tension, σuc in compression), and that σY in the formulas stands for that limiting strength when the material is brittle.
